title: Async/await — concept map
intro: C# async is a language transformation over Task and ValueTask: you write sequential statements, the compiler builds a state machine, and I/O completions resume you without occupying a thread. This module covers the Task-based Asynchronous Pattern (TAP), exceptions, cancellation, ConfigureAwait, IAsyncEnumerable, and how Tasks compare to JavaScript Promises.

overviewDiagram.title: Async method lifecycle
overviewDiagram.source:
flowchart TD
  A[Call async method] --> B[Returns Task immediately]
  B --> C{Hit await?}
  C -->|I/O incomplete| D[State machine suspends\nthread released]
  D --> E[I/O completes]
  E --> F[Continuation resumes\non pool thread]
  F --> C
  C -->|Done| G[Task completes\nresult or exception]

conceptCards.title: Why async
conceptCards.summary: async frees threads during I/O waits. It does not make CPU work faster. Blocking .Result wastes pool threads.
conceptCards.example: await sqs.ReceiveMessageAsync(url, token) — thread serves other work while waiting

conceptCards.title: Task and ValueTask
conceptCards.summary: Compiler rewrites async methods into state machines. ValueTask avoids Task allocation on sync-complete paths. Await ValueTask once.

conceptCards.title: Async exceptions
conceptCards.summary: Exceptions fault the Task, not the caller's stack. async void has no Task — exceptions go unobserved. Only for UI events.

conceptCards.title: CancellationToken
conceptCards.summary: Cooperative flag, not preemptive. Pass host StoppingToken into every await. Link with per-operation timeouts.

conceptCards.title: ConfigureAwait
conceptCards.summary: Controls where await resumes. Libraries use ConfigureAwait(false). ASP.NET Core has no SynchronizationContext.

conceptCards.title: IAsyncEnumerable
conceptCards.summary: Streaming async sequences with await foreach. Use EnumeratorCancellation for host shutdown. Avoid ToListAsync on huge streams.

conceptCards.title: Promises vs Task
conceptCards.summary: Same programmer model, different scheduler. JS microtasks on one thread; C# continuations on pool threads.
